exposure: Pharmacological treatment for depressive disorders during pregnancy
cohort: The study participants included 281 pregnant women with depressive disorders and 200 depression-free, healthy pregnant women, all of whom delivered their babies at Sant'Anna Hospital of Turin.
finding: Pregnant patients with depressive disorders are expected to have poorer outcomes compared to healthy controls, and pharmacological treatment for depression is associated with a reduced rate of cesarean section without inducing other maternal or newborn complications.
mod_finding: Women with depressive disorders showed higher rates of cesarean section, but pharmacological treatment was associated with a reduced rate of cesarean section.
